sights.address: Universal Studios Japan, 2-1-33 Sakurajima, Konohana-ku, Osaka
sights.w: The world's first Super Nintendo World opened inside USJ on 18 March 2021 (Mario Kart: Koopa's Challenge, Yoshi's Adventure); the Donkey Kong Country expansion (Mine Cart Madness) opened 11 Dec 2024 and grew the land by ~70%. Timed-entry via the USJ app on busy days.
sights.anime: Nintendo — Super Mario & Donkey Kong; the first Nintendo theme-park land anywhere, built in Osaka

sights.address: Hyōgo Prefectural Awaji Shima Park, Awaji, Hyōgo
sights.w: Anime theme park opened 15 July 2017 inside Awaji Shima Park: Naruto & Boruto, Dragon Quest, Crayon Shin-chan, SPY×FAMILY attractions and a life-size Shin Godzilla you zip-line into (Godzilla Interception Operation, 2020). Park entry free; attractions ~¥2,000–6,000. ~90 min by highway bus from Osaka.
sights.anime: Naruto · Godzilla · Dragon Quest · Crayon Shin-chan — Kansai's only multi-franchise anime theme park

sights.w: Kitty-head-shaped Sanrio complex on the Seto Inland Sea: an underwater Hello Kitty princess digital-art show plus two restaurants serving on Kitty tableware; the Hello Kitty Show Box (live musical lunch) is a short bus ride away.
sights.anime: Sanrio — Hello Kitty; the Kansai counterpart to Tokyo's Puroland

sights.w: Home stage of the all-female Takarazuka Revue. Osamu Tezuka grew up nearby and his mother took him here; the Revue's male-role stars, costumes and big sparkling eyes shaped Princess Knight and his whole art style. Pair with the Tezuka Manga Museum a short walk away.
sights.anime: Osamu Tezuka — Princess Knight (Ribbon no Kishi) was directly inspired by the Takarazuka Revue

sights.n: Haruhi Suzumiya pilgrimage — Kissa-ya Dream (珈琲屋ドリーム), Nishinomiya
sights.address: Kōfūen 1-chōme, Nishinomiya, Hyōgo (about 1 min from Nishinomiya-Kitaguchi Station)
sights.w: Author Nagaru Tanigawa is from Nishinomiya and the SOS Brigade's café is this real kissaten; Nishinomiya was named an Anime Tourism 88 pilgrimage site (2019 edition) with plaques at the café and the Nomura Securities branch. Fans hang Tanabata decorations here every summer.
sights.anime: The Melancholy of Haruhi Suzumiya — the SOS Brigade's meeting café; Nishinomiya = Anime Tourism 88 seichi (2019)

sights.n: Niteko Pond & Grave of the Fireflies memorial (Nishinomiya)
sights.w: The pond and hillside where Seita and Setsuko shelter in Akiyuki Nosaka's story (Ghibli film 1988); a 'Grave of the Fireflies' memorial stone was erected in June 2020 in the adjoining Nishinomiya earthquake memorial park. Cherry blossoms in spring.
sights.anime: Grave of the Fireflies (Studio Ghibli, Isao Takahata) — the real setting of the siblings' pond-side shelter

sights.w: Neo-Renaissance red-brick hall completed 1918 with a donation from stockbroker Einosuke Iwamoto (design Tatsuno Kingo & Okada Shin'ichirō); restored 1999–2002 and designated an Important Cultural Property in 2002. Free basement history exhibit.

1,300-year-old Umeda shrine named for Sugawara no Michizane's dew-and-tears poem; nicknamed after Ohatsu, heroine of Chikamatsu's 1703 'Love Suicides at Sonezaki', set in its grove — now a matchmaking power spot.

Temple founded by Gyōki in 744; its wooden main hall (rebuilt 1808) miraculously survived the WWII air raids amid the Minami neon. Appears in Chikamatsu's Sonezaki Shinjū and the rakugo story 'Mameda'.

CLOSED: Dōtonbori's neo-Renaissance theatre (opened 1923 as a cinema, kabuki/stage house since 1997) gave its final performance, the 'Onagori Gogatsu Ōkabuki', on 26 May 2026 after 103 years; Shochiku plans to demolish the ageing building. Facade-only now — no shows.

sights.address: Namba 1-chōme (corner lot west of Hōzen-ji), Chūō-ku, Osaka
sights.w: The only museum anywhere with a permanent display of Kamigata (Osaka-Kyoto) ukiyo-e — realistic kabuki-actor prints of stars like Nakamura Utaemon III, ~30 works over four small floors, plus print-making classes (reservation). Free with the Osaka Amazing Pass.

sights.address: Minami-Horie, Nishi-ku, Osaka (3 min from Yotsubashi Station)
sights.w: 800 m street that began as an Edo-era furniture town; now indie Japanese labels, vintage furniture and clothes, and open-air cafés beside old craftsman furniture shops. Time Out ranked it the world's second-coolest street (2025).

sights.address: Namba Sennichimae, Chūō-ku, Osaka (between Doguyasuji and Nankai Namba)
sights.w: Grid of narrow lanes south of Sennichimae around Sennichi Jizōson-dōri: standing bars, retro izakaya and young owner-run joints from Okinawan to Chinese, plus the bar-packed Misono Building.
